parameter_note: Placeholders are ${name}, the same textual substitution catalogue::render already performs for LSQB. String parameters carry their quotes IN THE TEXT ('${firstName}') because the renderer does not add them -- which makes a value containing an apostrophe, and LDBC's name corpus has them, a BROKEN statement rather than a wrong one. A renderer must REFUSE such a value rather than escape it quietly; an arm that binds natively (Bolt, libpq) should do that instead and ignore the quoting entirely. The VALUES are not in this file and must not be invented. LDBC curates substitution parameters precisely because uniform sampling over a skewed social graph spreads runtimes across orders of magnitude, and the curated files name Datagen's SPARSE original ids while this corpus is renumbered densely per label family. docs/bench/ldbc-coverage-plan.md section 2.1 has the translation plan (snbparams.rs), which does not exist yet. IS1-IS7 have no parameter files at all -- the official driver derives short-read parameters from earlier query results -- so those must be derived deterministically and stamped as derived.
projection_note: Every entry declares projection (column names and types, in order), order_by (the sort keys AS THE REFERENCE WRITES THEM, including keys that are not projected -- see IC5) and limit. Two dialects returning the same rows in a different order are not the same query, and SNB pins these orderings precisely because ties decide which rows survive the LIMIT. Null ordering is left at each engine's default and is believed to agree: Neo4j sorts nulls last on ASC and first on DESC, which is also PostgreSQL's default. That is read from documentation, not executed here, and it is load-bearing for IS3, whose sort key is null on every row of a store loaded by today's loaders.
corpus_note: Written for the corpus datagen2jsonl produces: ids are DENSE integers per label family from 0, Post and Comment share one Message id space, and the labels are exactly the ones the reference Cypher names -- Person, Message+Post, Message+Comment, Forum, Tag, TagClass, Organisation+University, Organisation+Company, Place+Continent, Place+Country, Place+City -- checked against datagen2jsonl.rs:407-471 rather than assumed. Datagen's original id survives as sourceId and is NOT indexed, so a parameter bound to sourceId is a label scan measuring something other than the query.
relationship_properties_note: Five of the twenty runnable reads project or filter a RELATIONSHIP property -- IS3 (KNOWS.creationDate), IC1 (STUDY_AT.classYear, WORK_AT.workFrom), IC5 (HAS_MEMBER.joinDate), IC7 (LIKES.creationDate), IC11 (WORK_AT.workFrom) -- and NO loader in this tree carries relationship properties (docs/bench/ldbc-coverage-plan.md section 0.3). /* IS2. Recent messages of a person
\set personId 10995116277795
 */
with recursive cposts(m_messageid, m_content, m_ps_imagefile, m_creationdate, m_c_replyof, m_creatorid) AS (
      select m_messageid, m_content, m_ps_imagefile, m_creationdate, m_c_replyof, m_creatorid
      from message
      where m_creatorid = :personId
      order by m_creationdate desc
      limit 10
), parent(postid,replyof,orig_postid,creator) AS (
      select m_messageid, m_c_replyof, m_messageid, m_creatorid from cposts
    UNION ALL
      select m_messageid, m_c_replyof, orig_postid, m_creatorid
      from message,parent
      where m_messageid=replyof
)
select p1.m_messageid, COALESCE(m_ps_imagefile, m_content, ''), p1.m_creationdate,
       p2.m_messageid, p2.p_personid, p2.p_firstname, p2.p_lastname
from 
     (select m_messageid, m_content, m_ps_imagefile, m_creationdate, m_c_replyof from cposts
     ) p1
left join
     (select orig_postid, postid as m_messageid, p_personid, p_firstname, p_lastname
      from parent, person
      where replyof is null and creator = p_personid
     )p2  
on p2.orig_postid = p1.m_messageid
order by m_creationdate desc, p2.m_messageid desc;

projection.type: STRING[] (DISTINCT; the reference imposes no order within the list)

/* Q13. Single shortest path
\set person1Id 8796093022390
\set person2Id 8796093022357

WITH RECURSIVE search_graph(link, depth, path) AS (
        SELECT :person1Id::bigint, 0, ARRAY[:person1Id::bigint]::bigint[]
      UNION ALL
          (WITH sg(link,depth) as (select * from search_graph) -- Note: sg is only the diff produced in the previous iteration

          FROM knows, sg x
          WHERE 1=1

          and k_person2id <> ALL (path)

          and not exists(select * from sg y where y.link = :person2Id::bigint)
          -- skip reaching persons reached in the previous iteration
          and not exists(select * from sg y where y.link = k_person2id)
        )
)

select depth from search_graph where link = :person2Id::bigint
union select -1) tmp;
